summary: Customer asks whether fiber optic products can measure line pressure and flow rate of a slurry in a transfer pipe and give an early warning of pipe blockage. The enquiry states no measurand values, no slurry properties, no pipe details and no performance targets, so no method choice can be made yet.

unknowns: Which physical quantity the customer actually needs for each target: static line pressure, differential pressure, flow rate (volumetric or mass), and what signal would define 'blockage'.
Measurement ranges, units and required accuracy for line pressure and flow rate.
Slurry composition: liquid phase, solids type, particle size distribution, solids concentration, and whether it is abrasive or corrosive.
Optical behaviour of the slurry: transparency, turbidity, colour, and whether it is opaque due to scattering.
Whether any optically detectable species or indicator is present (no fluorescent target named).
Process temperature and the pressure range of the line.
Pipe material, internal diameter, wall thickness, and whether the pipe is existing or new (retrofit constraints).
Installation point, access, distance from instrument to measurement point, and whether a fiber link is required.
What 'early warning' means: what precursor signal, how many seconds/minutes of lead time, and how false alarms would be handled.
Required response time and update rate for pressure, flow and blockage warning.
Fouling, scaling, sedimentation or coating risk at any window, probe or sensor in contact with the slurry, and cleaning method.
Environmental and site constraints: hazardous area classification, ambient temperature, vibration, ingress protection.
Reference or existing measurement method used today for pressure, flow and blockage detection.
Whether the customer requires a fiber optic solution specifically or any suitable measurement technology.
